description:
We’re a team of two students who share an interest in space, technology, and learning by actually building things. We’re still gaining experience, but that’s part of what makes this project exciting for us. We wanted to take on a challenge where we could learn new skills, work with real data, and turn an idea into something tangible.

For the NASA Space Apps Challenge, we’re working on identifying locations on Earth that could serve as analogs for potential permanent bases on the Moon and Mars. We’re exploring the problem through Earth and space science, data analysis, technology, and AI, with the goal of making the information easier to understand and interact with.

We’re approaching this project as both a competition and a learning experience. We’re experimenting, researching, building, making mistakes, and improving along the way. Since we’re a small team, we’re handling different parts of the project ourselves while learning as we go.
summary:
Paradigm Shift is an interactive platform designed to find places on Earth that have environments similar to those on Mars and the Moon. We developed a web-based demo that brings together planetary and Earth observation data to compare temperature, terrain and geological features. It aims to help users explore potential Earth analog locations, understand why they may be similar to other planetary environments, and examine the evidence behind each match.

This project addresses the challenge by looking beyond already-known analog sites and exploring the possibility of finding new locations using scientific data. It is important because studying similar environments on Earth can help researchers prepare for future space missions, test exploration methods and better understand the challenges of working on the Moon and Mars..
details:
Paradigm Shift — Discovering Earth's Planetary Analogs

What does the project do?

Paradigm Shift is an interactive planetary analog exploration platform developed for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. It investigates how Earth's extreme environments can serve as analogs for understanding the Moon and Mars.

The platform brings together geographical exploration, candidate discovery, environmental evidence, climate-data retrieval, planetary reference visualizations, and terrain-analysis capabilities in one browser-based application.

How does it work?

Users can explore Earth through an interactive 3D globe and geographical maps, investigate potential analog locations using the candidate-scanning workflows, and examine environmental evidence.

The platform also provides dedicated Moon and Mars exploration modes, allowing users to investigate planetary reference imagery and elevation visualizations.

Its Evidence workspace provides access to climate information through NASA POWER and Open-Meteo ERA5. Users can investigate temperature and precipitation information and compare environmental characteristics.

Additional capabilities include searching for geographically tagged ground photographs and performing numerical terrain analysis using compatible imported NASADEM HGT elevation tiles.

What benefits does it provide?

Paradigm Shift brings multiple planetary analog exploration capabilities together in one accessible interface. Instead of investigating geographical, environmental, and planetary information separately, users can explore these different perspectives within a single platform.

It provides a starting point for researchers, students, and space enthusiasts to investigate terrestrial environments that may offer useful insights for future lunar and Martian exploration.

Intended impact

Our goal is to make planetary analog exploration more accessible, interactive, and evidence-oriented.

By connecting Earth's extreme environments with lunar and Martian reference information, Paradigm Shift aims to encourage further investigation into geological fieldwork, environmental comparison, resource utilization, and the preparation of future space exploration missions.

Tools and technologies

The application was developed using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, with Three.js for interactive 3D visualization and Leaflet for geographical mapping.

External resources and services include NASA POWER, NASA GIBS, NASA Mars Trek, lunar planetary reference resources, Open-Meteo ERA5, Wikimedia Commons, and compatible NASADEM elevation files.

GitHub was used for source-code hosting and version control, while GitHub Pages was used to publish the application.

Creativity and innovation

The creative aspect of Paradigm Shift is its combination of Earth exploration and extraterrestrial planetary reference environments within one interactive research experience.

It connects potential analog discovery with geographical visualization, environmental data retrieval, and planetary comparison. This allows users to move from exploring a location on Earth to investigating its potential relevance to lunar and Martian environments.

Factors considered

The project considers environmental conditions, geographical context, terrain characteristics, data availability, planetary reference information, and the importance of scientific transparency.

We also considered the limitations of available datasets, differences between visual reference layers and numerical measurements, and the need to distinguish preliminary screening results from scientifically validated conclusions.

Paradigm Shift is an exploratory research prototype. Its candidate rankings are not validated probabilities of analog suitability or mission safety. Climate information from NASA POWER and ERA5 is reanalysis-based, and numerical terrain analysis requires compatible imported elevation data.
